### Observed differences

- In the later window, A09 occurs far more often within a case: about 4.3 occurrences per case on average versus about 1.9 before (about 6 versus about 3 among the cases containing it, which make up about 68 in 100 cases versus 62 before). Its self-pairs within five steps are observed in 115 cases versus 68 and now cluster at the two-event distance, and it is interleaved with A13 more often (co-occurrence about 68 versus 62 in 100 cases; interleaved-or-repeated about 60 versus 39 in 100). [OCC009, LAG016, REL013]
- In the later window, A03, A14 and A11 no longer repeat: each falls from about 2 occurrences per participating case to exactly one (recurrence shares of about 28, 28 and 15 in 100 fall to 0), with A03 and A14 appearing in about 47 in 100 cases (about 50 before) and A11 in about 47 in 100 cases (about 28 before). [OCC003, OCC011, OCC014]
- The A03/A11/A14 group also changed in composition and placement: before, A03 and A14 always co-occurred (about 50 in 100 cases) but A11 joined only about half of those cases, and the members were typically interleaved or repeated; in the later window all three always co-occur (about 47 in 100 cases) with no interleaving, both strict directions still occurring (A11 before A03 in about 33 in 100 cases versus A03 before A11 in about 14; A11 before A14 in about 39 versus 9), with short gaps (A14 then A03 within one event in about 68 in 100 observed pairs versus about 15 before; A03 then A11 within one event in about 61 versus 14) and earlier median positions (A11 about 0.11 versus 0.40; A03 0.17 versus 0.36; A14 0.20 versus 0.32 of the case's event sequence). [REL008, REL010, REL017, LAG010, LAG012, LAG035, POS002, POS004, POS006]
- In the later window, A15 appears in fewer cases (about 53 versus 62 in 100) but repeats more within them (about 4 versus 3 occurrences per participating case, with self-gaps shifting to the two-event distance), and its observed outgoing transitions lead to A09 in about 95 in 100 (about 41 before, with A01 about 38, now unobserved); A13's outgoing transitions similarly lead to A09 in about 71 in 100 (about 35 before), and A15 now also occurs without A09 or A13 (about 15 in 100 cases, previously never observed). [OCC015, LAG045, DIR015, DIR013, REL015, REL020, REL006]
- Smaller shifts in the later window: A06 occurs more often (about 1.13 versus 0.92 per case) and leads to A01 in about 99 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 86 before); A07 and A10 now appear in all cases (A07 in about 95 in 100 before); A01 repeats slightly more (about 4.2 versus 3.8 per case) with self-gaps concentrated at three events (about 20 versus 7 in 100), and A15 is no longer observed among A01's successors; A11 gained observed predecessors from A02, A05 and A08 (about 11–14 in 100 of those sources' outgoing transitions, unobserved before) and its own outgoing shifted from A03 and A14 toward A12 and A01. [OCC006, DIR006, OCC007, OCC010, OCC001, LAG001, DIR001, DIR002, DIR005, DIR008, DIR011]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that repetition within cases was reorganised. In the later window, A09 repeats about twice as intensively (about 3 to about 6 occurrences per case containing it, with self-pairs clustering at two events), while A03, A14 and A11 stopped repeating entirely (about 2 occurrences per participating case before, exactly 1 after) and now always occur together — A11 moved from covering about half of the A03/A14 co-occurrences to all of them — earlier in the case and in strictly ordered, though not single-direction, pairwise sequences. The signs are direct and consistent across occurrence, relation, position and gap indicators, and the activities involved are well observed in both windows (94–135 cases each). About half of the 103 evidence items exceed the 95th reference percentile — roughly ten times the about 5 expected for this many tests if nothing had changed, with 33 items at the maximum strength of 0.995 (a difference larger than in all 200 random re-splits) — so the pattern as a whole is unlikely to arise from sampling variability alone. [OCC003, OCC009, OCC011, OCC014, REL008, REL010, REL017, POS002, POS004, POS006, LAG010, LAG012, LAG016, LAG035]

Limitations: the evidence contains no screening expectation, so the chance comparison rests on the strength distribution rather than a reported baseline; positions and gaps are measured in event order, not clock time, so "earlier" means earlier in the case's sequence of events; the disappearance of interleaving in the A03/A11/A14 group largely follows from the repetition stop and does not by itself establish a new fixed sequence, since both directions still occur; and the evidence cannot rule out that the two windows simply sampled different mixes of the process's existing behaviours rather than a modified process. [REL008]

Other differences: A15's routing narrowed sharply (to A09 in about 95 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions, from about 41), A13's similarly (about 71 in 100, from about 35), A15 participates in fewer cases and now occurs without A09 or A13, and A09 interleaves with A13 more than before; A11 gained observed predecessors from A02, A05 and A08 and its outgoing shifted toward A12 and A01; A06 increased and now leads almost exclusively to A01; A07 and A10 became present in all cases; and A01 repeats slightly more with A15 no longer observed as its successor. [DIR015, DIR013, OCC015, REL015, REL020, REL006, REL013, DIR002, DIR005, DIR008, DIR011, OCC006, DIR006, OCC007, OCC010, OCC001, DIR001]
